metadata.rules_text:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < -0.3) — model is overly optimistic in such contexts.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (sentiment > 0.5) over 3–5 days, model tends to overreact and overforecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — fails to fully correct after sharp moves, especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially after volatility spikes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -0.3 to -0.7), model underperforms and should be scaled down.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — model often overcorrects after initial spikes, leading to premature peak forecasts.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending toward neutral, model tends to average out, missing sharp directional moves.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a dip, model often fails to recognize the breakout — should be adjusted upward by 5–10% in such cases.
